==English==

===Etymology===
{{nonlemma}}

===Pronunciation===
* {{enPR|grā'tə(ɹ)|a=UK}} {{IPA|en|/ˈɡɹeɪtə/}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈɡɹeɪtɚ/|[ˈɡɹeɪɾɚ]|a=US}}
** {{audio|en|Greater-pronunciation-us.ogg|a=US}}
* {{audio|en|LL-Q1860 (eng)-Vininn126-greater.wav|a=US}}
* {{rhymes|en|eɪtə(ɹ)|s=2}}
* {{homophones|en|grater}}

===Adjective===
{{head|en|adj}}

# {{en-comparative of|great}}; of [[two]] (or, rarely or non-standardly, more than two) [[thing]]s, [[larger]] in [[size]] ([[bigger]]), in [[value]], in [[importance]] etc.
#: {{ant|en|lesser}}
#: {{ux|en|While the north of the country has been dry, there is a '''greater''' need for rain in the south.}}
## {{n-g|In plant and animal names, denotes a larger kind.}}
##: {{ux|en|[['''greater''' yellowlegs]]}}
##: {{ux|en|[['''greater''' celandine]]}}
## {{n-g|Denotes the larger geographic or [[administrative]] area that [[encompasses]] or belongs to a place (especially if both share the same name).}}
##: {{coi|en|[['''Greater''' Antilles]]}}
## {{lb|en|usually|capitalized}} {{n-g|Denotes inclusion of the surrounding urban areas and [[conurbation]] (of a city or other large settlement).}}
##: {{coi|en|[['''Greater''' London]]}}
##: {{ux|en|'''Greater''' New York includes adjacent parts of three states, as well as the City itself.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=1990|author=Chikara Higashi; Geza Peter Lauter|title=The Internationalization of the Japanese Economy|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=qUPA2H1LSi8C|isbn=0792390520|page=285|text={{...}}statistics revealing that while '''greater''' Tokyo has a total area that represents only 3.6 percent of the total land available{{...}}more than 25 percent of the country's population live there.}}
##* {{quote-book|en|year=2004|author=Janet Golden; Richard Alan Meckel; Heather Munro Prescott|title=Children and Youth in Sickness and in Health: A Historical Handbook and Guide|isbn=0313330417|page=201|text=The rate in isolated counties was about a third higher than in the '''greater''' metropolitan counties.}}
##* {{quote-book
|en
|year=2013
|author=[[w:Peter Newman (environmental scientist)|Peter Newman]]; Anne Matan
|chapter=The Renewable Energy City
|title=Green Urbanism in Asia: The Emerging Green Tigers
|url=
|ISBN=978-9814425476
|LCCN=2012046043
|OCLC=832330332
|page=41
|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=1EQjyKa5PP4C&pg=PA41
|text=In February 2010, the largest high—concentration photovoltaic (HCPV) solar power plant in Asia began operation in Lujhu, located in the '''Greater''' Kaohsiung area.}}
##* {{see more citations|en}}
## {{ux|en|Denotes a state at its fullest historical (or desired future) extent including [[colonies]], [[annexed]] land, etc.}}
##: {{coi|en|[['''Greater''' Armenia]]}}
